newsitem.title: FRANCE: Moslem guerrillas kill 29 in Algeria - papers.
newsitem.headline: Moslem guerrillas kill 29 in Algeria - papers.

text.p: Suspected Moslem guerrillas have killed 29 civilians in Algeria in the past few days, including 17 bus passengers caught at a rebel roadblock, Algerian newspapers reported on Tuesday.

A band of up to 60 guerrillas killed 17 passengers travelling in two separate buses caught in a rebel roadblock near the southern town of Sfid, some 400 km (250 miles) south of Algiers, on Sunday night, said al Khabar newspaper.

"Seven passengers were shot dead before the eyes of all the travellers while the 10 others were dragged away and then were killed by having their throats cut four km (2.5 miles) away," said al Khabar without giving more details.
It was the latest in a series of killings of bus passengers in the past three years.
Violence in the conflict pitting the Algerian government against Moslem fundamentalist rebels has claimed about 60,000 lives over the last five years.
One of the most prominent victims was trade union leader Abdelhak Benhamouda, shot dead in central Algiers on January 28.
On Monday night a Moslem fundamentalist said on Algerian state-run television that his guerrilla group had killed Benhamouda.
Moujahed Rachid, a 30-year-old university student, said one member of his seven-member group, Kamal Boulanouar, shot the union leader as part of a plan to throw the country into political crisis.

"Our programme focused on assassinations which would have great impact prompting a crisis at the level of the government. The killing of senior personalities had a significant impact", he said in a pre-recorded interview broadcast on Monday night.
Algerian newpapers reported on several weekend killings. The bodies of five people kidnapped a few days ago were found in Algiers on Saturday, said Liberte newpaper.
Four women, including one shopping in a market, were killed on Saturday and Sunday in separate attacks in Algiers, it said.
Two people were killed in Boufarik, 30 km (20 miles) south of Algiers, on Monday when a bomb exploded in a market, said Le Matin newspaper.
The Algerian security forces said in a statement quoted by Algerian state-run radio one person died in the blast and 13 were wounded.
A hairdresser was shot dead on Sunday in Bab el Oued, a Moslem fundamentalist stronghold in central Algiers, said Le Matin.
"These assassinations coincided with an Armed Islamic Group (GIA)'s statement announcing the resumption of deadly attacks in Algiers and Blida," said Le Matin.
Algeria's ruthless GIA said in a statement published on Monday that it had launched a new wave of killings.
